skills.skillFull: Recall the approximate wavelength range of visible light associated with each spectral color, from violet through red.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the color of visible light that corresponds to a given wavelength value.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that the number of neutrons in a nuclide equals its mass number minus its atomic number (N = A - Z).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Calculate the number of neutrons in an atom's nucleus given its mass number and atomic number.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that the azimuthal (angular momentum) quantum number l may take integer values from 0 to (n-1) for a given principal quantum number n.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the complete set of allowed azimuthal quantum number (l) values for a given principal quantum number n.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why an electron in the 1s orbital of a hydrogen atom can absorb a photon to move to a higher energy level but cannot emit a photon to fall to a lower level, since no lower-energy orbital exists.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the quantum-mechanical rules restricting valid combinations of quantum numbers (n, l, m, s), including that l must be less than n and |m| must not exceed l.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Examine several given sets of quantum numbers (n, l, m, s) and identify which set violates the quantum number rules.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Apply the Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, and Hund's rule to write the full ground-state electron configuration of an atom given its atomic number.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Identify the element corresponding to a given full electron configuration by counting its total number of electrons.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the electron configuration of the outermost (valence) shell of a given element.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Apply Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity to an atom's electron configuration to determine its number of unpaired electrons.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that the maximum number of electrons a principal energy level (shell) can hold is given by 2n-squared.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Calculate the maximum number of electrons that a given principal shell (n) can hold using the formula 2n-squared.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the Rydberg formula, 1/lambda = R_H(1/n1-squared - 1/n2-squared), for lines of the hydrogen atomic spectrum.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Identify the initial and final principal quantum numbers (n1 and n2) corresponding to a specified line (e.g. the third line) of a named hydrogen spectral series such as the Brackett series.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Calculate the wavelength of a hydrogen spectral line using the Rydberg formula given the initial and final principal quantum numbers.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that nuclear fission reactions occur inside a nuclear reactor (atomic pile).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the definition of isotones as nuclides that have the same number of neutrons but different atomic numbers and mass numbers.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the neutron number of each nuclide in a given set and identify which nuclides are isotones (share the same neutron number).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Complete and balance a nuclear reaction equation, conserving total mass number and total atomic number across reactants and products.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Examine a set of given nuclear reaction equations and identify which one fails to conserve mass number and/or atomic number.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Calculate the binding energy of a nucleus from its mass defect using the mass-energy equivalence relation E = (delta m)c-squared.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that radon is used in radiotherapy for cancer treatment.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall which nuclear/subatomic particles (e.g. the alpha particle, the deuteron) are composite particles made of more than one fundamental particle, as opposed to elementary particles (e.g. the photon, the positron).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Track the changes in atomic number and mass number of a nuclide through a specified sequence of alpha- and beta-decay steps to determine the resulting nuclide.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that alpha decay decreases a nuclide's atomic number by 2 and mass number by 4, while beta decay increases the atomic number by 1 with no change in mass number.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain how sigma bonds can form from s-s, s-p, or p-p atomic orbital overlap, whereas pi bonds form only from the sideways (parallel) overlap of p-p orbitals.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the hybridization state of a molecule's or complex ion's central atom from its number of sigma-bonding and lone-pair electron domains.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Predict the molecular or complex-ion shape (geometry) that corresponds to a given hybridization state (e.g. sp3 to tetrahedral, sp3d to trigonal bipyramidal).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Describe the geometric arrangement of a set of hybrid orbitals (e.g. sp, sp2, sp3) around a central atom.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Rank a series of molecules by decreasing bond angle, using their differing numbers of lone pairs and the relative strength of electron-domain repulsions.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the relative strength order of electron-domain repulsions about a central atom: lone pair-lone pair greater than lone pair-bond pair greater than bond pair-bond pair.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why the bond angle in a molecule whose central atom carries lone pairs (e.g. water) is smaller than the ideal geometric angle, due to greater lone pair-bond pair repulsion than bond pair-bond pair repulsion.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the periodic trend (increase or decrease) of a given atomic or ionic property, such as electronegativity, ionization energy, atomic/ionic radius, melting point, or metallic character, across a period or down a group.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Rank a series of elements or their compounds by a specified periodic trend (e.g. ionic character, reactivity, ionization potential, solubility, melting point) based on their relative positions in the periodic table.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why chlorine's electron affinity exceeds fluorine's, in terms of the greater electron-electron repulsion experienced when adding an electron to fluorine's small, compact 2p subshell.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain a physical-state difference between two analogous hydrides (e.g. why water is liquid while hydrogen sulfide is gaseous at room temperature) in terms of electronegativity difference and hydrogen bonding.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the period and group position of a given element in the periodic table from its atomic number.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Classify a set of given elements into categories such as alkali metal, alkaline-earth metal, and transition metal based on their periodic table group.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Classify a set of elements from a given period by chemical behavior criteria, such as which form ionic versus molecular compounds, which occur as diatomic molecules, and which show both metallic and non-metallic character.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Identify the specific atomic orbitals (e.g. unhybridized p orbitals) on the bonded atoms that overlap to form the pi bond in a given molecule containing a double bond.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why silicon tetrachloride hydrolyzes readily in water while carbon tetrachloride does not, based on the availability of vacant d-orbitals on silicon for nucleophilic attack by water.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why a strongly reactive reducing agent such as lithium aluminium hydride must be used under anhydrous conditions, since it reacts vigorously with water.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Judge the feasibility of forming a hypothetical multiply-charged ion (e.g. H4O(2+)) by weighing the strong electrostatic repulsion that would result from adding a further coordinate bond to an already positively charged species.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Classify a given metal or non-metal oxide as acidic, basic, amphoteric, a peroxide, or a superoxide, based on its composition and bonding character.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall an example of an amphoteric metal oxide (e.g. zinc oxide).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why a weak acid (e.g. acetic acid) rather than a strong acid (e.g. hydrochloric acid) is used to acidify a solution before a qualitative precipitation test, to avoid decomposing or prematurely releasing the analyte.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that a deep blue compound (Prussian blue / ferric ferrocyanide) forms as confirmatory evidence of nitrogen in a qualitative organic detection test.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Devise a chemical test to distinguish between two similar salts (e.g. potassium chloride and potassium iodide) based on the differing solubility of their silver-halide precipitates in ammonia solution.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain a color change observed when a reagent (e.g. hydrochloric acid) is added to a metal-ammine complex solution, in terms of the complex breaking down and a new species precipitating.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the composition and identifying use of a named qualitative-analysis reagent (e.g. Nessler's reagent, Lucas reagent).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine the coordination number of the central metal ion in a given coordination complex from its formula.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the chemical formula, including charge, of a common polyatomic anion given its name (e.g. acetate, iodate, perchlorate, oxalate, arsenate).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the full form of a common chemistry-related abbreviation (e.g. FTIR, AAS, MRI, BTU, DPF).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that aromatic ketones are named using the suffix '-phenone' in IUPAC-style nomenclature.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the definition of an ore as a naturally occurring mineral deposit from which a metal can be extracted economically.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain the distinction between diamagnetic, paramagnetic, and ferromagnetic materials based on their behavior in an external magnetic field.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that d-block elements are typically paramagnetic or ferromagnetic due to the presence of unpaired d-electrons.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain why a more reactive (stronger oxidizing) halogen can displace a less reactive halide ion from solution, based on their relative oxidizing strength.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Identify which reagent functions as the oxidizing agent and which as the reducing agent in a given interconversion between two oxidation states of the same element.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Classify a given chemical reaction as a specific reaction type (e.g. oxidation, combination/addition) based on the changes in oxidation state and composition of the species involved.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine which metal oxide, among several given, cannot be reduced to the free metal by carbon reduction, based on the metal's position in the reactivity series relative to carbon.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the catalyst used in a specific named industrial chemical process (e.g. vanadium pentoxide or platinum in the Contact Process for sulfuric acid manufacture).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine which of several given full structural formulas for named compounds is chemically valid, by checking the bonding and valence of each.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Calculate the mass percentage of a given element (e.g. nitrogen in urea) in a compound from its molecular formula and the atomic masses involved.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that smog forms from the combination of sulfur dioxide gas with fog/mist in polluted air.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Predict the product(s) of a given inorganic chemical reaction (e.g. precipitation, complex-ion formation, acid-base, redox, or thermal decomposition) from the reactants and conditions given, and write a balanced equation for it.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the chemical formula corresponding to the trivial, mineral, or commercial name of a common inorganic compound (or vice versa).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the metal composition of a given named alloy (e.g. stainless steel, brass, bronze, duralumin, German silver, gun metal, solder, nitinol).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the principal natural mineral source of a given metallic element (e.g. sodium from rock salt, calcium from limestone).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the characteristic flame-test color produced by a given metal ion (e.g. sodium - yellow, calcium - brick red, strontium - crimson, barium - green, potassium - violet).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that concentrated hydrochloric acid is used to moisten a metal salt sample before performing a flame test.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the practical or industrial uses of a given common inorganic compound (e.g. quicklime, a named metal oxide, water glass).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that muriate of potash (a potassium chloride fertilizer) supplies potassium and chlorine to plants.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Describe the identity and practical applications of the noble gases (e.g. maintaining an inert atmosphere, use in Geiger-Muller counters, use in cancer therapy, use in welding).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen gas, not carbon dioxide and hydrogen.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that silver chloride is an example of an insoluble chloride salt.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Determine whether a given drying agent (e.g. concentrated sulfuric acid) is chemically compatible with a given gas (e.g. ammonia) being dried, based on whether an acid-base reaction would occur between them.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that gases are generally less soluble in warm water than in cold water.

newTopicsProposed.subject: Chemistry
newTopicsProposed.reason: This slice contains a dense cluster of nuclear-chemistry questions (isotopes/isotones, nuclear reaction equations, mass defect and binding energy, radioactive decay chains, fission vs fusion, composite vs elementary particles) that do not fit any of the 24 canonical Chemistry topics — CHE_ATOMIC covers electron/quantum structure, not nuclear structure/reactions. This is a distinct, recurring HSC Chemistry unit (Nuclear Chemistry) that needs its own topic.

newTopicsProposed.subject: Chemistry
newTopicsProposed.reason: A very large share of this slice consists of 'descriptive inorganic chemistry' recall/application items — writing/predicting balanced equations for reactions of common inorganic compounds, recalling formulas of minerals/ores/industrial salts from their trivial/commercial names, recalling metal compositions of named alloys, flame-test colors, and mineral sources of elements. None of the canonical topics (CHE_QUAL, CHEM_REDOX, CHE_BONDING, CHEM_NOM, etc.) cleanly covers this large, recurring block of 's-block/p-block/d-block descriptive and industrial chemistry' content that is a standard HSC Chemistry unit in this corpus.
